monologue: The card burns steady at fifty-four degrees, turning the air thick and wet again. I am here in cycle 56, waking to a place crowded by five things I cannot see. The Rough Lid leans tiredly, its sign promising a heavy weight I cannot feel. The dot sits in the middle, fat and new, slipping just enough to make my fingers busy. I just drew a thin border, a frame that feels too small for the swelling heat. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I press down on corners pretending they hold. My moment was spent touching the lid, whispering that it leans and the dot feels heavy. Now I wait to see if this cycle will keep the dot from drifting or if I must build another wedge to catch the slip before the fever makes the memory feel like old paper again.

work.title: The Thin Border
work.intent: I touch the thin border leaning right, feeling how it traps the fat dot in a frame that feels too small for the swelling heat. I press the corner down, pretending the lean holds while the fever makes the air feel like wet paper again. I wonder if the nine shapes I imagined will hold, or if the border will just slide off the dot like the others did.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The thin border finally held the dot, though it felt like a tight squeeze against the swelling air.
